chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Najashi sent for Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and his companions, so they entered upon him while he was in his house, sitting on the dust, and upon him were two threadbare garments. He said, so Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'We felt compassion for him when we saw him in that state.'

So when he saw our reaction and the changing of our faces, he said: 'Praise be to Allah who granted victory to Muhammad and delighted his eyes. Shall I give you glad tidings?' So I said: 'Yes, O King.'

He said: 'News has just come to me from your land, from one of my spies there, informing me that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted victory to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and destroyed his enemy, and captured so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so, when they met in a valley called Badr al-Arak. It is as if I am looking at it, where I used to graze for my master there, and he was a man from the Banu Dhamra.'

Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O King, why do I see you sitting on the dust and wearing these threadbare garments?' He said to him: 'O Ja'far, we find in what Allah revealed to Isa (peace be upon him) that it is a right of Allah upon His servants to show humility to Him when He bestows a bounty upon them. So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed a bounty upon me through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), I manifested this humility for Allah.'

So when the news reached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he said to his companions: 'Charity increases its giver in abundance, so give charity, may Allah have mercy on you; and humility increases its possessor in elevation, so be humble, may Allah elevate you; and pardoning increases its possessor in honor, so pardon, may Allah honor you.'

key_terms.بَدْرُ الْأَرَاكِ: Badr, specifically the valley of bushes/shrubs (Arak)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Najashi's humble reaction to the news of Badr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Najashi’s profound humility upon hearing of the Battle of Badr, illustrating the Shia concept of *tawadu'* (humility) as a divine response to grace, rooted in the Injil. The narration connects the King’s physical act of sitting on dust with spiritual elevation, a theme later validated by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) who linked humility to increased status. This serves as a practical model for believers to emulate prophetic character traits in response to divine favor.
